President Bola Tinubu on Thursday congratulated former President Goodluck Jonathan as he marks his 69th birthday on Friday, November 20. Tinubu described the former Nigerian leader as “a patriot and statesman whose commitment to national unity, democratic governance and Nigeria’s peaceful advancement remains an important part of the country’s political history.” Tinubu conveyed his felicitations in a statement signed by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. The president acknowledged Jonathan’s progression through successive tiers of elected office from Deputy Governor and Governor of Bayelsa State, through the Vice Presidency under the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, to the presidency itself. He also commended his continued engagement in peace, mediation, and democratic consolidation across Africa after leaving office. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “As Dr Jonathan celebrates this special occasion, President Tinubu wishes him continued good health, renewed strength, wisdom, and many more years of meaningful service to Nigeria, Africa, and humanity,” the statement read. Born on November 20, 1957, in Ogbia, Bayelsa State, Jonathan rose through academic and administrative ranks, holding a doctorate in zoology from the University of Port Harcourt, before entering politics as deputy governor in 1999. He became governor in 2005 following the impeachment of his principal, Diepreye Alamieyeseigha, and was elevated to the vice presidency in 2007 under Yar’Adua. Why I conceded defeat to Buhari without resistance — Jonathan Tinubu confers GCON on Wole Olanipekun 2027: Stakeholders plan Tinubu re election campaign in Bayelsa When Yar’Adua died in office in May 2010, Jonathan was sworn in as president, winning a full term in 2011 before his tenure ended after the 2015 general election. Defeated by former General Muhammadu Buhari in the contest widely regarded as the most competitive in Nigeria’s post-military history, Jonathan reportedly placed a congratulatory phone call to Buhari before the final results were announced, conceding defeat. Since leaving the Presidency, Jonathan has pursued an active career in conflict resolution and electoral mediation. He has served as a special envoy of the Economic Community of West African States and led observer and mediation missions in Liberia, Senegal, and other West African states grappling with political instability. His work through ECOWAS has included efforts to persuade military-led transitional governments in the Sahel, most notably Mali, to commit to credible electoral timelines. Jonathan has also been a vocal advocate for the use of technology in electoral administration as a tool for improving the credibility of African elections.
